newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Dec 28 Initial Claims from 366,000; Dec 28 Four-Week Average from 352,500; Dec 21 Continued Claims from 2,558,000 and Dec 14 from 2,456,000.
Wall Street economists had forcast initial jobless claims of 353,000 in the January 4 week.
The department said the four-week average of claims for the week ended January 4 was the highest since an average of 360,500 in the week ending July 13, 1996.
The department said 22 states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended December 28, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Michigan, with 24,588 additional jobless claims, Wisconsin with 17,784, Pennsylvania with 10,425, Massachusetts with 8,371 and Kentucky with 8,204.
Michigan said its rise in claims was due to holiday shutdowns in industries throughout the state. Wisconsin had layoffs in transportation, construction, trade, services and manufacturing.
Pennsylvania saw layoffs in transportation, trade, food and manufacturing, while Kentucky had layoffs in lumber, textiles and electrical equipment. Massachusetts did not provide a reason.
Labor said seven states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the December 28 week.
Among the largest were Texas with 9,021 fewer claims filings, Virginia with 5,551 and Colorado with 3,235.
Texas said it had fewer layoffs in trade, services, apparel, non-electrical machinery and the electrical and transportation equipment industries.
Virginia attributed its decrease to the shorter workweek due to the Christmas holiday and to fewer layoffs in food, textiles, apparel and rubber industries. Colorado did not provide a reason.
